channel.title: Jayesh Suryavanshi · Writing
channel.description: Technical studies and field notes on machine learning, LLM agents, and the models I take apart.

item.title: The browser is a peripheral
item.description: Claude Code can drive Chrome, and the documentation covers what it can do without saying how. Reading the shipped binary, the extension bundle and the tool server’s own session logs turns up five hops from tool call to page, two transports where I expected one, a screenshot frame that disagrees with its own declared scale, and the part where your page text leaves the machine. Prefer references to pixels, and assume every returned string was written by the page.

item.title: The empty classroom
item.description: A deep learning professor at IISc Bangalore put down his prepared lecture and spent the hour asking his students why they still come to class. He is also one of the people automating the answer away: no more research assistants, his own learning moved to an LLM, and a teaching skill built from his lectures on his company's marketplace. Why a builder's alarm is worth more, not less, and where his supporting numbers slip.

item.title: The unmapped majority
item.description: Coverage honesty for geotagged social data. Most pipelines map the 1-2% of posts with exact coordinates and call it the geography; count the coverage first and 84% carry no location at all. A worked example with GeoSocialX: place-resolution recovers 10x more than exact coordinates alone, fuller but coarser, and the honest move is to report the hole rather than hide it.

item.title: Informative but subsumed
item.description: What news text really adds to unrest forecasting, measured on a leakage-controlled benchmark: 336M events, 55 countries, and a text-signal ladder up to neural embeddings of 1.37M headlines. The semantics of news are already in the event record; the small real complement is the arithmetic of coverage.

item.title: The closed frontier, mid-2026
item.description: GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8 and Fable 5, and Grok 4.5: who actually holds the crown at the closed frontier, and why nobody holds all of it. Adversarially fact-checked: two of five headline claims came back qualified.

item.title: The open-weights frontier, mid-2026
item.description: Inkling vs GLM 5.2, Kimi K2.7, DeepSeek V4, and Nemotron 3 Ultra: a benchmark-checked field guide to who actually wins what, and how far the open tier has closed the gap to the closed frontier.

item.title: Inkling, up close
item.description: A close read of Thinking Machines Lab's 975B open-weights multimodal MoE: what's actually new in the architecture, where it really lands on benchmarks, the real-time system it was built for, and how I'd fine-tune it on Tinker.
